title: CRLA/134/2010 of PRAMOD LAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No.134 of 2010
Pramod Lal,
S/o Sri Jashmal Lal,
R/o Village-Dalsinghi,
Patwari Circle-Chandrapuri,
Tehsil-Ukhimath,
District Rudraprayag. .......Appellant (In Jail)
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand. .......Respondent
Mr. Rajesh Sharma, Amicus Curiae for the appellant.
Mrs. Mamta Bisht, learned A.G.A., Ms. Sangeeta Miyan and Mr. P.S. Danu, learned
Brief Holders for the State.
Dated: May 24, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
This appeal, preferred under Section 374 (2) of
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short Cr.P.C.), is
directed against the judgment and order dated
28.05.2010, passed by the Sessions Judge,
Rudraprayag, in Sessions Trial No. 03 of 2010,
whereby the said court has convicted the accused/
appellant Pramod Lal under Sections 363, and 376 of
I.P.C. The accused/appellant Pramod Lal has been
sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for a period of five
years and directed to pay fine of ` 5,000/, and in
default of payment of fine further simple imprisonment
for a period of six months under Section 363 of I.P.C.,
and has been sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for a
period of seven years and directed to pay fine of
` 5,000/, and in default of payment of fine further
simple imprisonment for a period of six months under

2
Section 376 of I.P.C. All the sentences shall run
concurrently.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the lower court record.
3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that on 19.12.2009
an F.I.R. was registered by the Asadu Lal (father of the
victim) with the Police Station, Jakholi, district
Rudraprayag, in which he stated that on 17.12.2009,
his daughter Benazir disappeared from the house. He
tried to search for her at his relatives' place, but she
could not be found. She was also searched on
18.12.2009, but she was not found. He reported that
some people of Mayali told him that Pramod, who owns
a Band Baja Shop at Mayali, has taken his daughter
with him. In the report, he requested to lodge an F.I.R.
against the accused Pramod. The said F.I.R. was
registered at 11:00 p.m. On the basis of said report,
Chik report (Ex. A-2) was prepared and the case was
registered in respect of offences punishable under
Sections 363, 366 and 376 of I.P.C., against the
accused Pramod. The medical examination of the
prosecutrix was conducted on 22.12.2009 at 02:45
p.m. Thereafter, the accused was arrested on
22.12.2009 at 11:00 p.m. After completion of
investigation, the Investigating Officers submitted
charge sheet against the accused Pramod Lal, for his
trial in respect of offences punishable under Sections
363, 366 and 376 of I.P.C.

3
4. After hearing the parties on 08.04.2010, learned
Sessions Judge, Rudraprayag, framed charge of
offences punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376
of I.P.C, to which the accused Pramod Lal pleaded not
guilty and claimed to be tried. On this, prosecution got
examined P.W. 1 Benazir (the victim), P.W. 2 Asadu Lal
(complainant), P.W.3 Mrs. Munni Devi (mother of the
victim), P.W.4 Head Constable Sanjay Lal, P.W.5
Ramesh Chand (maternal uncle of the victim), P.W.6
Dhan Pal Singh Bhandari (In-charge Nayab Tehsildar),
P.W.7 Dr. Yashoda Pal (Medical Officer) and P.W.8
Buddhi Raj (Investigating Officer). Oral and
documentary evidence was put to the accused under
Section 313 Cr.P.C., in reply to which he alleged that
the evidence adduced against him is false. After
hearing the parties, the trial court found accused
Pramod Lal guilty of offence punishable under Sections
363 and 376 of I.P.C., and convicted him accordingly.
Aggrieved by judgment and order dated 28.05.2010,
passed by the Sessions Judge, Rudraprayag, in
Sessions Trial No. 03 of 2010, this appeal is preferred
by the convict.
5. P.W.7 Dr. Yashoda Pal, medically examined
Benazir (the victim), on 22.12.2009 at 02:45 p.m. In
the medical report (Ex. A-8), she gave following
observations:
"No injury marks on breast seen. No
external injuries marks seen over body.
In Genital examination:

4
Pubic hair present. No external injury
marks present on genitalia. No
discharge or secretion seen around
genitalia. Hymen was not intact.
Secretion seen coming through vaginal
opening. It was dirty white discharge.
Pubic hairs collected, two slides of
vaginal secretion prepared and sealed
and sent for pathological examination"
In the said report, the Medical Officer opined that
hymen was not intact. Girl was not habitual for
intercourse. Pregnancy could not be ruled out at that
stage. No supplementary medical examination report
has been placed on record.
6. P.W.1 Benazir (the victim) stated on oath that on
17.12.2009, when she was going from her house to
Jakholi, in order to see the fair, then on the way Santu
met her. She told her that she was going to Mayali and
asked her to accompany her till there. She further
stated that both of them went to Mayali together, after
which Santu left for her work. Thereafter, the accused
Pramod Lal met her. She stated that she was not
knowing him from before. He identified himself as
Pramod Lal. He told her that he owns a Band Baja
Shop at Mayali and asked her where she wanted to go.
She said that she intended to go to Jakholi to watch
the fair. Then, he informed her that the said vehicle
was leaving for Jakholi and asked her to sit in the said
vehicle. She sat in the vehicle, but the vehicle instead
of going to Jakholi took her to Chaura. She stated that
she had no idea to whose house she was being taken.
The accused Pramod Lal came in the room at 12:00
midnight where she was kept. When he entered the

5
room, he held her by her chest, opened her lower
clothes and committed rape on her. She stated that she
screamed, cried and resisted his attempts, but he
closed her mouth, after which she could not scream
anymore. She also stated that she was raped thrice
that night after which she fainted. Next day, at around
04:00 a.m. in the morning, he told her that he will drop
her at her home, but instead he took her to Tilwara.
She stated that she did not know to whose house she
was taken at Tilwara. She stated that she was kept at
Tilwara on 18th and 19th and the accused committed
rape on her even there. He threatened to kill her if she
raised a hue and cry and also said that if she remained
silent, he will drop her to her house. On 20th, the
accused told her that he will drop her to her house, but
he took her towards Augustmuni instead, where her
maternal uncle Ramesh Chandra saw her and asked
her. Then, she narrated the entire incident to him.
Thereafter, her maternal uncle telephoned her father,
after which her father and the Nayab Tehsildar reached
on the spot and arrested them and took them to
Jakholi.
7. P.W.2 Asadu Lal (complainant) is the father of the
victim. In his statement, he has stated that in the
morning of 17.12.2009 at 07:00 a.m., he went for his
work to Bajra village. His daughter Benazir was at
home and his wife had gone to her maternal house. He
stated that his wife came back home on the very day at
around 04:00 p.m., and when he came back from
work, then his wife asked him the whereabouts of their

6
daughter. At this, he told his wife that children told
him that Benazir had gone to see the fair. He stated
that when on 17th his daughter did not come back
home, then they searched for her, thinking that she
might have gone to some relatives place. When on
18.12.2009 also, the girl did not return, then he along
with his son went to Mayali market to search for her.
There some people told him that his daughter had gone
with Pramod, who owns a Band Baja Shop at Mayali.
This witness has said that he also enquired about her
here and there, after which he was convinced that
Pramod had ran away with his daughter. This witness
has also stated that his daughter is minor, aged 14
years.
8. P.W.3 Mrs. Munni Devi is the mother of the
victim. She has reiterated the statement given by
P.W.2. In addition, she has stated that her daughter
told her that Pramod Lal has committed rape on her. In
her cross-examination, this witness has stated that the
age of her elder son is 28 years. Age of her second
daughter is 23 years. This witness has further said
that the age of her third child is 22 years and the age
of her youngest daughter is 14 years and she studies in
school. This witness has stated that the difference
between the age of third male child and fourth female
child is 4-5 years.
9. P.W.4 Head Constable Sanjay Lal stated that the
accused Pramod Lal had been arrested on 20.12.2009,
who escaped from custody eventually. After which, the
case was filed against him.

7
10. P.W.5 Ramesh Chandra is the maternal uncle of
the victim. He stated that on 18.12.2009, his brother-in-law Asadu Lal informed him about the
disappearance of his daughter Benazir and on
20.12.2009, he saw her at Augustmuni market with a
boy and upon enquiring further, she told him about
the said incident.
11. P.W.6 Dhan Pal Singh Bhandari and P.W.8
Buddhi Raj are the Investigating Officers. In their
statements, they have stated that they had not taken
the prosecutrix for radiological examination in order to
determine her age.
12. P.W.7 Dr. Yashoda Pal medically examined
Benazir P.W.1 on 22.12.2009. In her statement, she
reiterated the same version, which she had written in
the medical report. In addition to her statement, she
stated that she did not get conducted any medical
examination in respect of determining the age of the
prosecutrix. She also stated that at the time, when the
medical examination of the victim was conducted, she
was normal and no symptoms of rape or intercourse
were found.
13. Learned Amicus Curiae for the appellant
submitted that there is delay in filing the First
Information Report. He submitted that the prosecutrix
was missing from 17.12.2009 and the First Information
Report was registered two days' after i.e. on
19.12.2009. He submitted that had the case of
abduction of the victim been there, the family members

8
of the prosecutrix would have lodged the F.I.R. earlier.
He further submitted that there is contradiction in the
statement of the prosecutrix as well as in the statement
of her father and mother. He then submitted that in
fact, the prosecutrix was not kidnapped, but she, by
her own sweet will, went along with the
accused/appellant and no case under Section 363 of
I.P.C. is made out against the accused. He argued that
the prosecution has not brought any documentary
evidence on record, which could suggest the age of the
prosecutrix and in fact, contradiction is found in the
statements of the prosecutrix as well as of her mother
and father, and if the statement of the mother of the
victim is to be believed, the prosecutrix on the day of
incident was 18 years of age. He contended that in fact,
no rape was committed on Benazir, which finds
support from the evidence of the doctor. He further
submitted that on the basis of these arguments, the
appellant is entitled to be acquitted from the charges
levelled against him.
14. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. for the State
submitted that though it is true that there is two days'
delay in lodging the First Information Report, but when
a girl is missing from her house, normally, family
members of that girl search for her in her friends and
relatives house and thereafter, the family members
think about lodging an F.I.R. She submitted that in the
present case also, on 17.12.2009, when the father of
the victim came back home, then he was informed that
his daughter has gone to Jakholi, in order to see the

9
fair. He must have thought that his daughter will
return back in the night. But when she did not return
back home by the next day, he enquired about her in
his relatives place and only thereafter, on 19.12.2009,
the First Information Report was lodged.
15. I find force in the arguments of the learned A.G.A.
for the State and thus, delay in filing the First
Information Report is sufficiently explained by them.
16. For proving the case under Section 363 of I.P.C.,
the prosecution is required to prove that Benazir was
kidnapped from lawful guardianship. First of all, let us
examine the age of the prosecutrix from the material
available on record. I find that though the age of the
prosecutrix is shown as 14 years at the top of the
medical examination report, but still the doctor had not
sent her for further medical examination for
determining her age. From the statements of the
Investigating Officers also, I find that they did not take
any step for sending the girl for medical examination in
order to determine her age. Nothing has been brought
on record by the prosecution, which could suggest
about the age of the prosecutrix. Only thing, which is
said by the prosecutrix herself in her examination-in-chief, is that she is 14 years of age. Neither any school
certificate nor any birth certificate issued by the Gram
Pradhan was produced by the prosecution in support
of the age of the prosecutrix. In the cross-examination,
the prosecutrix has stated that her elder brother is
Surender Lal aged 28 years. After him is her elder
sister Rinki and then her brother John Major and after

10
him, she herself. She has stated that her elder sister is
8-9 years elder than her and is 2-3 years younger than
Surender Lal. A closer scrutiny of the statement of the
prosecutrix reveals that the age of prosecutrix was
about 18 years. Similarly, the mother of the victim has
stated in her testimony that the age of her elder son is
28 years. In second number, there is her daughter
aged 23 years. In third place is her son aged 22 years,
but in her cross-examination, she has stated that the
age of her younger daughter is 14 years and is
studying in school. The father of the prosecutrix has
also stated that his daughter is 14 years of age and is
studying in school. Thus, it is clear from the
statements of the mother and father of the victim that
the prosecutrix was studying in school, but still no
attempt was made to bring on record any school
certificate, which could suggest the age of the
prosecutrix.
17. Thus, from considering these facts, it would not
be in the interest of justice to draw inference that at
the time of incident, prosecutrix was about 14 years of
age and punish the appellant. Rather, considering the
statements of the prosecutrix and her mother, it
appears that the prosecutrix was about 18 years of age.
Nothing is on record on which basis inference can be
drawn that the prosecutrix was below sixteen years at
the time of incident. The Medical Officer also in her
testimony has stated that no injury marks were seen
on the breast of the prosecutrix. From the statement of
the prosecutrix, I nowhere find that she was forcefully

11
taken from one place to another. In my view, she has
voluntarily gone from one place to another. Though,
she has stated in her statement that she was raped by
the accused/appellant, but the statement of the doctor
does not support the statement of the girl. The doctor,
in her statement, has stated that at the time, when the
medical examination of the victim was conducted, she
was normal and no symptoms of rape or intercourse
were found.
18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the
present case, I find that the prosecution has failed to
prove the case beyond reasonable doubt. In such
circumstances, the appellant is entitled to the benefit
of doubt.
19. Consequently, the appeal is allowed. Impugned
judgment and order dated 28.05.2010, passed by the
Sessions Judge, Rudraprayag, in Sessions Trial No. 03
of 2010, is hereby set-aside. The accused/appellant
Pramod Lal is acquitted of charges of offences
punishable under Sections 363 and 376 of I.P.C. He is
in jail. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the
Superintendent of the Jail concerned, who may set the
appellant at liberty forthwith, if he is not wanted in
connection with any other crime. Let the Lower Court's
Record be sent back.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Arpan 24.05.2013
